headline: Agents Are Eating Design Systems
subheadline: Brad Frost is talking about agentic design systems, Figma's MCP ecosystem keeps maturing, and Claude Code just shipped a meaty update — all directly relevant to what you're building.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Agentic Design Systems in 2026 with Brad Frost
sections.description: Brad Frost explores how AI agents are now consuming design systems — assembling UIs from your components autonomously. This is exactly the trajectory your white-label sport apps system is on. His framing of design systems as APIs for agents could reshape how you architect tokens and components for both human designers AND AI consumers.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: AI in 2026: Five Product Shifts We'll Have to Design For
sections.description: Olena Zanichkovska argues that what slows AI down isn't capability but product design — unclear decision logic, fragile trust, poor workflow integration. As someone moving toward product leadership, this is the strategic lens you want. It reframes AI limitations as design problems, which is exactly your superpower.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma's 2026 Updates Redefine Design-Dev Handoff
sections.description: Designers can now branch, commit, and merge Figma files directly to GitHub/GitLab — version history links to commit hashes. This is a big deal for your Figma MCP + Claude integration work. If your design system files can be versioned alongside code, the handoff story for your white-label apps gets dramatically tighter.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Claude Code: Week 15 Release Notes (April 6–10)
sections.description: Fresh Claude Code update: worktree switching, PreCompact hook blocking, background plugin monitors, and improved MCP handling. The MCP reliability fixes matter directly for your Figma MCP integration — better stream and network handling means fewer dropped connections when Claude is reading your design system context.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: AI in Design Systems: What's Changing in 2026
sections.description: Zeroheight maps the current state of AI + design systems — from token management with AI to automated documentation and GitHub PR workflows. Good validation of the direction you're already heading with your MCP project, and might surface patterns you haven't considered for token syncing.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: OpenAI Codex + Figma Integration via MCP
sections.description: OpenAI's Codex now connects to Figma through MCP servers, letting developers use Figma context for design-informed code generation. Worth knowing about as a competitive reference — see how they've structured the Figma-to-code pipeline compared to your Claude-based approach. Could reveal architectural ideas worth borrowing.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Design systems as execution layers for AI agents
sections.description: The emerging mental model: your design system isn't just a library for humans — it's an API that AI agents call to assemble interfaces. This means token naming, component contracts, and documentation quality directly affect how well an agent can build with your system. The teams treating design systems as machine-readable contracts are pulling ahead.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If agents consume your design system, what needs to change?
sections.description: Your white-label sport apps design system was built for human designers. If AI agents are now assembling UIs from those same components — are your token names semantic enough? Are component props self-documenting? Is there metadata an agent needs that a human never did? Stroller walk thought material. 🎧
